Style guide v2 (final) for the new EVE Women and Fertility Clinic website, 6 October 2026. Built from the client's picks on the v2 review board: Hero B, Find care B, Why EVE C, Meet your doctor A and First visit A. Colours and type are the locked v1 tokens. Hover, click, scroll and swipe to try everything.

Build notes for the coding agent · read before building
  • Locked Fonts: Figtree (all UI and text), Instrument Serif italic (one accent word per heading, at most), Noto Sans Devanagari (only if Hindi or Bodo text appears). Load with next/font, self-hosted, preload only Figtree.
  • Locked Colours: copy the :root tokens in this file exactly. --glow and --accent are decorative only. --blush-100 and --blush-50 are washes only. --rose is used only for the italic serif accent word and small heart marks.
  • One gradient surface per viewport: primary buttons, the active tab, the Book button and the mobile bar. Everything else is white with tints.
  • Hero (changed in v2): portrait on the left, text on the right. Dr. Swati is a background-free cut-out (transparent PNG and WebP) set on a slowly changing blush shape, with one continuous sage line, drawn from the logo's mother-and-child line, that wraps around her and ends in a small rose heart. The line draws once on load and the heart beats twice; the photo itself never animates in. A drawn placeholder stands in until the shoot; the photo spec is under the hero.
  • Find care (new): a plain-language list of eight concerns directly under the hero, each linking to its page.
  • Why EVE, Meet your doctor, First visit: bento with a journey tile; editorial doctor profile with qualification seals and a path; steps with a sticky guide card on the right that plays one small illustration per step.
  • Motion: slow, plays once per view or drifts in the background, never moves text being read. Everything stops under prefers-reduced-motion; autoplaying rows keep a pause button.
  • Mobile: any section with more than three cards becomes a self-moving swipe carousel below 768px (every 4.5s, pause on touch or hover, pause button, still under reduced motion).

headroomcrop at waist
Photo spec for the cut-out
  1. Pose: waist-up, shoulders slightly turned (about 15 degrees) toward the text side, so on desktop she faces the headline. Natural smile, white coat open over a plain top.
  2. Background: plain light grey or white wall, with her standing a metre or more away from it, so hair edges separate cleanly. No busy clinic backdrop.
  3. Framing: leave space above the head and keep both shoulders and elbows in frame. The design crops at the waist.
  4. File: at least 3000 px tall from the camera. The cut-out is delivered as transparent PNG and WebP, 1600 x 2080 (the 400 x 520 ratio used here), with clean hair edges and no white halo.
  5. Build: preload this one image (it is the main hero image). The shape and the line animate; the photo itself never fades or slides in.

Colour · locked

Sage, blush and deep moss

Sage is the logo's own line colour and blush is its background, so the site feels like an extension of the mark. Deep moss gives contrast and weight, as Oliva does with its dark Book button. Rose is the single warm accent, kept for the italic heading word and soft glows. The palette stays calm, clinical-safe and clearly for women's health, without the sugary pink of a baby brand.

Do

  • White page background everywhere; tints only for chips, tabs, washes and glows
  • Blush washes behind glass cards and the doctor section, so the blur reads and the page feels warm
  • One gradient surface per viewport
  • Sage text #4F6445 for links and eyebrows, so they pass on tints too
  • Rose #A24560 for the italic accent word, one per heading at most
  • Red only for "Medical emergency? Call 108 or 112" and the emergency callout

Do not

  • Pure black text, or grey text lighter than #55655B
  • Logo sage #5C7450 for small text on tints (fails 4.5:1)
  • Blush, sage light or blush rose for any text
  • Pink buttons, pink gradients or hot pink; rose is an accent, not a surface
  • Green, orange or other colours not in this palette (WhatsApp green only on the WhatsApp button)
  • A red cross or red plus anywhere, or baby-brand imagery
  • Dark full-width hero panels (Oliva's dark hero is not used; ours is white with glows)
Logo

EVE logo in use

Full logo on white in the header (max 56px tall desktop, 44px mobile, because the wordmark is wide). White version on the gradient (mobile menu header, footer band, OG images). The mother and child mark alone is for the favicon and app icon. The supplied PNG has a blush background; the versions here are cut to transparent.

For Windsurf: the logo arrived as a PNG, so the edges are soft at large sizes. Redraw it as SVG, keeping the single-line mother and child mark, the EVE WOMEN & FERTILITY CLINIC wordmark and the "By Dr Swati Shree" script tagline. Make a full set (sage, white) and a mark-only version for the favicon. Submit the SVG set for approval in Phase 1. Do not recolour the wordmark.

01 / Why EVE

Time, honesty and options

Bento layout over a blush tint. "One doctor throughout" is the large deep-moss tile, where a small dot travels the patient's path with the same doctor at every step. When the section comes into view, the other cards' icons each make one small move: the clock hand turns, the lens looks around, the chat dots blink. Text never moves. Facts only.

03 / How we can help

Care for every stage, every question

Clean white service cards on the plain page: the illustrated badge, the service name, one line, and a View service link. No window shapes or moving backgrounds. Hover: the card lifts, the orbit ring spins once around the badge, the badge turns like a coin and the arrow fills. The row moves on its own and pauses on hover or touch.

04 / Your first visit

Your first visit, step by step

Steps on the left, a sticky guide card on the right. As you scroll, the card shows the step number, a small line illustration that plays once, and the progress rail, with the Book button always close. Each step carries a few practical details as chips. Click a step or scroll the page.

Callouts

Medical page notices

When to get help straight away. Call 108 or 112, or go to the nearest hospital emergency, if you have very heavy bleeding, sudden severe pelvic or abdominal pain, fainting, or any bleeding with pain during pregnancy.

Medically reviewed by Dr. Swati Shree, MBBS, DNB (OBG), MRCOG (UK) · [CONFIRM: State Medical Council registration no.] · Last reviewed [CONFIRM: sign-off date]

Tip. Many fertility checks are timed to your cycle. Note the first day of your last period before you call.
